reading_notes: Portfolio rule 5 ('Sharpe >= highest benchmark Sharpe - 0.20') is applied to the benchmarks the engine reports: equal_weight_hold, equal_weight_monthly, inverse_vol_monthly (cash assets excluded from it, since BIL's tiny volatility would make it nearly all cash) and sixty_forty when SPY and TLT are both held.
Any failed portfolio cell, including a trade-count miss, makes the idea 'rejected' (the memo says any miss = REJECTED).
Windows start with holdings carried in; engine 'entries' counts a position already open on the first day of a window as an entry.

H26 episodes = days the weight drops by at least 0.25 (the 1 -> 0.5 transitions); H27 position changes = entries + exits; H28 events = entries, and an event's net return is its three daily net returns plus the exit-day cost.
Overnight memo vetoes 'block SUPPORTED': a cell set that would be supported becomes 'testing'.
Calendar memo veto is a hard reject: in either window, 3 or more symbols with return per exposure day below buy-and-hold's mean daily return minus 5 bps.
Exit bars stay flat for H28 (no same-bar re-trigger); month-ends come from the exchange calendar.
